title: Coefficient order locus equals the extended Hilbert equality germ
statement:
Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, $U$ a smooth affine finite-type $k$-scheme, $X\hookrightarrow U$ a closed subscheme with coherent ideal, and $a\in X$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $N\subset U$ be smooth closed through $a$, with etale coordinates $w$ and regular equations whose transverse Jacobian is invertible. Write centered straightened Taylor variables as $(W,Z)$, so the Taylor ideal of $N$ is $(Z)$; $K_b$ denotes the Taylor ideal of $X$ at $b\in N$, over $L_b=\kappa(b)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Suppose $f_{i,b}=\sum_\gamma T_b(c_{i\gamma})(W)Z^\gamma$ have coefficients regular on one common $N$ and belong to $K_b$. Fix a monotone orthant diagram $D$ with ordered minimal vertices $(0,\alpha_i)$, degrees $d_i$, and first-vertex supports [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Require that the transverse variables $Z$ are precisely the essential variables of these vertices, namely those occurring with positive exponent in some $Z^{\alpha_i}$; in particular an empty vertex list has no transverse variables and $N=U$ near $a$. At $a$, suppose the $f_{i,a}$ have orders $d_i$, unique supported homogeneous division for every degree prefix, and supported generation of $K_a$, whose initial diagram is $D$. Fix $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$. For each degree block, let $Z^\ell$ be its accumulated essential variables and $s_\ell$ its last vertex. Assume for every $b\in N$ that one can choose vertex derivatives $g_j=\partial_Z^{\beta_j}f_{i(j),b}\in(Z^\ell)$, $\alpha_{i(j)}=\beta_j+e_j$, with invertible $Z^\ell$-Jacobian, and for $i>s_\ell$, $\partial_{Z^\ell}^{\beta}f_{i,b}\in(Z^\ell)$ whenever $\beta$ is in the restricted prefix diagram and $|\beta|\le Q$ [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative].
Define $S\subset N$ by $\operatorname{ord}_b c_{i\gamma}\ge d_i-|\gamma|$ for $|\gamma|<d_i$, and let $H_D(t)=\#\{\eta\notin D:|\eta|\le t\}$. Assume $a\in S$. There exists a neighbourhood $V$ of $a$ in $U$ such that
$$S\cap V=\{b\in V:H_{X/k}(b)=H_D\},\qquad H_{X/k}(b)(t)=\dim_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(b)[[T]]/(K_b+(T)^{t+1}),$$
using ordinary centered Taylor variables $T$ in $U$ outside $N$. This is the extended function, retaining all relative variables at nonclosed points.
More precisely, for sufficiently large finite $q\ge\max_i d_i-1$, the coherent ideal generated by cumulative Taylor-rank minors through degree $q$, formed from any regular generators of the ideal of $X$, equals near $a$ the ideal obtained by adjoining the equations of $N$ to the inverse image of the ideal on $N$ generated by the finitely many $\partial_w^\delta c_{i\gamma}$ with $|\delta|<d_i-|\gamma|$. Its Taylor extension at $a$ is
$$(\partial^\nu f_{i,a}:|\nu|<d_i)=(Z,\partial_W^\delta T_a(c_{i\gamma}):|\delta|<d_i-|\gamma|).$$
The minors here are the determinants of the submatrices expressing fibre-rank bounds [def-trf-minor-ideal]. Equality holds on a common neighbourhood as coherent ideals, rather than just as formal ideals at $a$. Empty vertex lists are allowed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-formal-low-derivative-coefficients] over the residue field of b0 to the coefficient family TN_b0(c_i,gamma), the prescribed expansion, and the central block hypotheses. The unital field map from k to this residue field transfers characteristic zero. This proves the final formal derivative/coefficient identity.

Apply [lem-trf-straightened-regular-stratum-comparison] to obtain a generating-list-independent cutoff q0, its vertex bound, the equality-locus open V for every q and list, and the formal extension map(straight)(J_q)=lowDerivativeIdeal.

Compose that extension identity with the formal coefficient identity and apply [lem-trf-coefficient-derivative-ideal-descent] to J_q. It yields an open W with equality of the actual regular ideal sheaves, and identifies the coefficient-order locus with vanishing of J_q.

Intersect V and W. Both contain i(a), using j(b0)=i(a). Compose the coefficient-order/vanishing equivalence on W with the vanishing/Hilbert equivalence on V. Pull back the ideal-sheaf equality on W along the inclusion V intersect W -> W; functoriality of comap identifies this with the required equality on the common open. Retain the two formal equalities unchanged. The construction covers all empty-list and zero-variable cases because each constituent statement does.

There are no new nodes, every cite is in unit sk-i-curve-zero, there is no SGA, uses equal proof_deps, and there is no cycle. Live is still unsplit and there is no repair note, so this is an ordinary first split. The delivery adds the hypothesis that the transverse Z are exactly the vertices' essential variables. The old statement is false without it: U=X=A^1, N={0}, D empty gives a Hilbert locus equal to U while S={0}, and the formal identity reads 0=(Z). The parent lem-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-data states this hypothesis, so its step 5 still applies. The cited formal-hilbert-stratum-minors node assumes the same essential-variables condition, so the repair also makes steps 1–2 valid. Step 1: H_a=H_D comes from jet-diagram, and r_t=rank B_t(0) because the columns span the image of K; the equality-locus germ comes from the finite-type clause of formal-minors. Step 2: the coordinate change is an invertible A-linear substitution, and the (r_t+1)-minors are Fitting ideals (k=H_D(t)-1≥0). Step 3 (elementary, correct): (g_j)=(Z)⊂E because U(0) is the Jacobian, and mod Z we get γ!∂_W^δ c_γ. Checked on z²+w³ (E=(z,w²), C=(w²)) and on z^d. Step 4: implicit-taylor's statement gives restriction as Z=0 evaluation, faithful flatness at nonclosed points, and spreading to a neighbourhood, so I=J. Step 5: injectivity of the normal-cone map gives ord_b c≥h iff T_b c∈(W)^h, and the derivative coefficients give V(C)=S. Step 6: the empty case gives N=U and J=0, and a degree-0 vertex is impossible. Overlap with the set-germ clause of lem-trf-formal-coefficient-transform-criterion is advisory only; that node cites the item's parent, so the item cannot cite it.
